overviewAccounting.derivedMapDisposition: The overview is a guide, not a navigation-type source. Its three integration/uncertainty teaching checks per pin reuse already verified chapter fields and give no new independent scientific credit. The concept-link list is routing only. Each index personal-context section is excluded without copying its text.

rows.requirement: Translate a broad platform claim into a population and treatment setting, specimen/method, measured or predicted outcome and proposed decision; keep unknown details blank.
A molecule measurement, drug ranking in a dish and prediction from earlier patients are different claims; define what best treatment is intended to mean.
Risk prediction needs a time horizon and care context; risk under usual treatment is distinct from untreated risk and from a guarantee about one person.
A drug-ranking proposal needs the actual drug, dose or combination and the relevance of experimental conditions to the proposed care.
Separate the measurement, biological interpretation, clinical prediction, proposed action and evidence of patient benefit; mark each measured, inferred, proposed or unknown.
A claim records tested material, quality requirements, a proposed mechanism and alternative biological explanations.
Prediction identifies outcome, population and period; action identifies what would change; patient benefit needs evidence against an alternative.
Record the exact laboratory, service, version and intended use; laboratory or research status does not replace claim-specific evidence.
Check any label-defined companion-diagnostic requirement separately from a report drug list; expedited development designation is distinct from marketing approval or test validation.
Retain the fictional protein/Drug A responder example: abundance measured in stored tumour, response association in treated advanced Cancer X and a proposed postoperative use are separate claims.
A treated-only response association does not establish differential treatment benefit versus an alternative, and advanced-disease evidence does not establish postoperative benefit.
Personalised wording closes neither comparison nor setting gaps; ask for evidence that choosing the drug with the result improves the proposed outcome and setting.
A broad predicts-benefit headline may hide a narrower response association; write the actual outcome and comparator.
A gene or target name alone does not establish treatment actionability.
A research result needs its producing service, method version and intended-use boundary before being treated as a clinical report.
A negative result depends on detection/quantitation limits, sampling time and pretest frequency; it does not establish that a condition is absent.
Separate the fictional earlier-recurrence-detection claim from the claim that a test-guided strategy improves survival; measured lead time needs detection dates and population.
Lead-time bias can extend survival measured from detection without postponing death; earlier detection alone does not prove survival benefit.
The explain-back exercise identifies protein measurement, postoperative Drug A addition and missing evidence of improved outcome as three separate answers.
Evaluation of the exact claim needs suitable data not used for development or tuning; a chart alone does not establish independent performance.
Trace the plot back to eligibility, participant selection, failed samples, outcome access during threshold selection and treatment context.
Perfect-sample-only performance may not transfer to real practice, and reusing training patients can reward memorisation or tuning.
External evaluation uses data outside development; compare sites, handling, calendar period and care. Independent data and evaluation matter more than a different company or institution logo.
An evidence card records cancer type, stage, treatment setting and selection, with any mismatch to the proposed group.
An evidence card records specimen, handling, method version and quality criteria; input changes may alter performance.
An evidence card records the reference standard or care comparator and its limitations rather than assuming it is infallible truth.
An evidence card names the outcome and measurement time; response, recurrence and survival are distinct endpoints.
An evidence card retains prespecification, all search/tuning choices and truly held-out evaluation; exploratory findings need confirmation that does not reuse their selection.
An evidence card retains failed specimens, dropout and missing outcomes so difficult cases do not silently disappear.
An evidence card includes sample size, intervals and remaining uncertainty; a point estimate is not a promise about one person.

Preclinical evidence states the actual model and tested claim. Nonassigned clinical care needs confounding assessment; neither alone validates a proposed action. Test evaluation and compound evidence are separate routes.

Analytical validation precedes an assay performance claim. The cited AMP/CAP sequencing-panel guidance is scoped to variant types, reference materials, depth and sample numbers, not every possible test.
Report the target level, detection probability, input and specimen behind a detection limit; the lesson uses a 95% convention that needs assay-specific justification.
Precision considers repeatability and conditions across days, operators and instruments; trending needs the measurement variation understood.
Accuracy assessment needs an appropriate independent reference or established method on matched material; self-agreement alone does not establish accuracy.
Report the proportion of attempted samples that yields no result and the reasons; success-only accuracy omits a real-world failure rate.
Validation includes specimen type, preservation, handling and interference; fresh-plasma performance does not automatically transfer to delayed samples.
PPV depends on condition frequency in the tested population as well as the stated sensitivity and specificity.
Retain the first fictional 1,000-person example: 10% condition frequency, 90% sensitivity and 95% specificity give 100 affected, 90 true positives, 45 false positives and 90/135, about 67%, PPV.
Retain the second fictional 1,000-person example: 2% frequency with unchanged sensitivity/specificity gives 20 affected, 18 true positives, 49 false positives and 18/67, about 27%, PPV.
The two-slide illustration retains every tuning choice on Hospital A, locking before B and B outcomes excluded from further tuning; show failures rather than inventing performance numbers.
Recomputing A can check computational reproducibility but is no new independent population test. B still needs relevant patients, failed-test denominators, uncertainty and calibration.
Verify the Michiels historical result at its actual scope: five of seven large microarray prognosis studies performed no better than chance under repeated random splits, not every model or assay.
A new hospital may still mismatch disease setting; risk discrimination/ranking and calibrated probabilities are distinct, and one universal performance cutoff cannot authorise every clinical use.
Even a well-calibrated prognostic risk score does not establish benefit from a treatment suggested beside it.
Retain attempted and reported denominators and failure reasons instead of reporting only successful samples.
A threshold needs its selection date, tuning history and independent test; a cross-disease dataset needs its mismatch stated.
Laboratory status cannot substitute for clinical evidence; false-positive and false-negative consequences depend on the action that follows.

The unchanged-Hospital-A practice answer requests data held out from every tuning choice, preferably an independent setting, plus locked method, population, outcome, failures and uncertainty; advanced treated risk ranking does not establish postoperative treatment selection.
The later version additionally distinguishes all assigned participants, those treated and only evaluable participants as treatment-study analysis populations; retain which denominator is used.
Begin with a named decision and distinguish a research-learning goal from a supported clinical action.
Specify actions for positive, negative, uncertain and failed results; if every branch leads to unchanged care, immediate clinical decision value is limited while a stated research goal may remain.
A useful result must arrive within the decision window; consuming finite tissue has opportunity costs for other assays.
The decision ledger names the treatment/trial decision and the action and evidence for positive, negative and uninformative results, including proposed omission or repeat/confirmation.
Compare existing pathology or alternative tests and account for specimen, time, travel, uncertainty and financial burden.
Name who interprets the result and owns the clinical recommendation and define a stopping rule; the worksheet exposes assumptions rather than calculating a treatment choice.
Retain the fictional postoperative Drug A/protein-assay case, whose treatment-selection evidence comes from another setting; access and transportability are separate questions.

Possible branches include checking the actual companion-diagnostic label, reviewing drug evidence, considering a matched trial or declining tissue-consuming testing that would not change the decision.
Confirmation asks whether the measurement is real; it does not establish whether the proposed intervention helps or turn abundance into proven postoperative benefit.
Drug approval elsewhere, clinician-led off-label use, access, payment and suitability are distinct; a report listing a medicine guarantees none of them.
A valuable research goal can test a mechanism, explain assay disagreement or generate a hypothesis without selecting treatment; name its reviewer and a useful answer to avoid endless testing.
Attribute unpublished company data and record what was available to inspect; unavailable evidence is distinct from proof that a claim is false.
Changing treatment after a test is not itself demonstrated benefit and can add unnecessary treatment.
A favourable prognostic result does not establish safe treatment omission. A new test can displace better-supported testing, and urgency cannot validate an unsupported action.

Retain the high/low recurrence-test exercise: if neither result changes care and no relevant study is open, weigh a separately stated research/personal-information goal against burdens, uncertainty and alternatives.
The explain-back answer retains positive, negative and uninformative branches, the evidence and clinical owner for each, and a plan for uncertainty.
A proposal needs the complete product, clinical setting, evidence and requested action; a target shortlist or recipe analogy cannot establish biological benefit or safety.
Reviewing data, consuming tissue, making a product and administering it are distinct commitments, each requiring a rationale and responsible owner.
The product proposal records disease setting, treatment intent, alternatives, measurable goal and the exact molecule or peptide-HLA target with specimen and method.
Assess target accessibility and selectivity with protein location and relevant normal-tissue data while retaining sampling limits.
Record the full binder/payload/cell design and mechanism and the relevant human comparison or explicitly limited preclinical evidence.
Record product-specific risks, monitoring, management capability and stopping rules; manufacture, release, sponsor, site and access pathway are separate readiness gates from the immediate decision.
ADC assessment asks how antibody, linker and payload act together and which delivery/resistance steps were tested; internalisation is design-specific rather than a universal yes/no requirement.

For an engager or cell therapy ask about CRS, ICANS and other neurological effects, healthy-tissue recognition, tissue access and what can persist after dosing stops; do not transfer CAR-product incidence to every engager.
A radioligand assessment connects imaging with the therapeutic product distribution, absorbed dose and organ limits. Tracer uptake alone supplies neither efficacy nor a CAR-T safety threshold.
A TCR therapy requires a specified peptide and HLA allele and evidence of specificity, presentation and function; receptor sequence or clonal expansion alone answers none of those completely.

Retain Product Q as a fictional specified ADC against surface protein M with a cleavable linker/payload, considered for progressing metastatic solid cancer after prior treatment; the immediate action is existing-data review, not manufacture, treatment or sampling.

The fictional dossier contains only one tumour-biopsy RNA result and cultured target-bearing-cell activity; human comparisons, surface measurement, healthy-tissue testing, supplier participation, access and site arrangements are absent or unknown.
The completed card retains Q identity, the metastatic setting, measured evidence and a research hypothesis rather than borrowing benefit from another M-targeted format.

The card retains missing accessible protein, healthy-tissue effects, full-product delivery and relevant human outcomes; a research lead reviews methods and controls first, consumes no tissue and pauses if product identity or usable evidence is unavailable.

Ask which Q-specific result would change experiment planning. RNA abundance is distinct from accessible surface protein, and protein confirmation would still not establish clinical benefit; the Mertins study measures separate RNA/protein layers, not surface access or treatment selection.
In the United States, an effective IND concerns the applicable investigational product/protocol and is not marketing approval; BLA submission is distinct from BLA approval.
A manufacturing quote does not establish all supply, consent, review, delivery and monitoring gates, and even confirmed access does not prove benefit.
Do not turn expression into benefit, one format into another format evidence, an experiment into a treatment commitment or speculative availability into future protection against recurrence.

Retain the second Q exercise after complete tumour removal: the new request is postoperative prevention plus manufacturing and administration, while evidence remains one biopsy RNA signal and cultured-cell activity.

Neither the attributed IND milestone nor supply offer closes the postoperative evidence gap; ask the clinical team for Q-specific evidence or a relevant protocol, the sponsor for covered product/protocol and the readiness owner for delivery gates.

With only the fictional dossier, evidence/pathway review is supported and manufacture or administration is not justified by it; the explain-back answer retains finding, product/setting, proposed commitment, missing clinical/safety evidence and answer owner.
